Dear Dr Jones,
Re: Mrs Katherine Walter,

DOB: 26 November, 1975

I am writing this letter to refer you Mrs Walter, a 40-year-old woman, whose features are suggestive of
depression and bipolar disorder. Your urgent assessment and treatment would be highly appreciated.

Mrs Walter is married and has two children. She is asthmatic and has been suffering from chronic fungal
skin infections in both feet since 1999. Her current medications are budesonide inhaler and clotrimazole.
Regarding her family history, she has a family history of moderate depression reported from her father,
sister, uncle, and aunt.

Comment [benchmark1]: Please note,

On 19/11/2014, Mrs Walter complained of feeling tired. On examination, nothing was remarkable.

On today's review, Mrs Walter attended my surgery complaining of feelings of not coping associated with
suicidal thoughts and the desire to die. Moreover, she reported that her sleeping habits are bad and she
feels tired, overwhelmed with her responsibilities as a mother and has no energy for her usual household
tasks. For example, she has no desire to eat, cook, clean, or take care of her offspring's. On examination,
her body mass index was 17, 3 which is lower than the normal range for her age. At this stage, her
husband was contacted in order to discuss child care and house hold maintenance.

In light of the above, I would be grateful if you could promptly assess and manage her condition, as you
think appropriate. Should be there any further queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
